newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals called to open mixed.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals called to open mixed.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were called to open mixed Tuesday, but gold failed to make any overnight follow-through gains from the advance in New York Monday.
COMEX June gold was called flat to off $0.50 from Monday's close of $344.30 an ounce.
COMEX July silver was called flat to off 0.5 cent from Monday's close of $4.768.
Traders said the bullish effect of the Bre-X scandal was ebbing. Attention was being paid to the stock market rally.
New York trading in precious metals Monday was quiet due to public holidays in Japan and the U.K.
Some analysts said Monday that because Bre-X's Busang deposit has turned out to be false, it had helped boost gold prices because a large amount of yellow metal would not now come on the market.
COMEX June gold traded $344.70 to $344.00 on ACCESS.
July silver traded between $4.785 and $4.765 on ACCESS.
Monday, COMEX silver stocks rose 2,346,326 ounces to 190,864,646 ounces, while COMEX gold stocks were unchanged at 946,012 ounces.
NYMEX July platinum and NYMEX June palladium were called to open $1.00 firmer.
